sections.title: Case and asthma phenotypes
notes: 6-year-old with eczema, allergic rhinitis, cough early morning and with play, clear lungs: **asthma**.
Transient early wheeze (under 1 year, outgrown), non-atopic early onset, late onset (over 3 years), persistent early onset (mostly atopic).
More common in boys before puberty, **more severe in girls after**.

sections.title: Asthma predictive index
notes: Predicts persistent asthma. **One major**: parental asthma, **eczema**, aeroallergen sensitization.
**Or two minor**: food sensitization, **eosinophils over 4%**, wheezing without colds.

sections.title: Pathophysiology
notes: Allergen, **IgE**, mast cells: edema, vasodilation, mucus, **bronchoconstriction**.
Plus inflammation (IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, eosinophils). Treat both: **bronchodilator plus anti-inflammatory (inhaled steroid)**.

sections.title: Triggers and symptoms
notes: **Viral infection is the most common trigger (rhinovirus)**. RSV or rhinovirus bronchiolitis raises later asthma risk.
Smoke (even outside), pollution, **NSAIDs, beta blockers**, exercise, pollen, pets, dust mites, cockroaches, mould, weather.
Wheeze, chest tightness (young kids call it chest pain), dyspnea, cough, **worse at night and early morning**. Forced exhalation brings out wheeze.

sections.title: Diagnosis
notes: Spirometry over 5 years: **low FEV1 with normal FVC**, scooped flow-volume loop. Exercise challenge for exercise-induced asthma.
Allergy testing for persistent asthma (pets, environment).
**Chest x-ray not needed**: hyperinflation, peribronchial thickening, **atelectasis often mistaken for pneumonia**.

sections.title: Exercise-induced asthma
notes: 15-minute **warm-up**, scarf or mask helps 80%.
**Salbutamol before exercise** protects 2 to 3 hours. Montelukast helps about 50% but takes hours.

sections.title: Follow-up and inhaler technique
notes: Reassess every 2 to 6 weeks at first, then every 1 to 6 months. Spirometry at start, 3 to 6 months later, then every 1 to 2 years.
**Inhaler technique is the most important step**: watch them use it.
**MDI with spacer works at any age**. Mask under about 3 years, mouthpiece over 5. **Dry powder inhalers not for under 5**.

sections.title: Beta agonists and inhaled steroids
notes: SABA (salbutamol): works in 15 minutes, lasts 3 to 4 hours. LABA (salmeterol, formoterol): 12 hours, **only with an inhaled steroid**.
New guideline: **add a LABA rather than doubling the inhaled steroid**.
Beta agonist side effects: tremor, tachycardia, **hypokalemia**, masked hypoglycemia in diabetes.
**Inhaled steroids are the best long-term controller** and improve lung function. Growth slows slightly but final height is reached. Rinse mouth (thrush). Osteoporosis with high doses.

sections.title: ICS-formoterol: MART and AIR
notes: **Only formoterol** (fast onset) can be the reliever in combination. Salmeterol can't.
**MART**: one ICS-formoterol inhaler as daily maintenance and as reliever. **AIR**: ICS-formoterol as needed only (anti-inflammatory reliever).
Max: 8 puffs a day ages 6 to 11, 12 puffs over 12.

sections.title: Montelukast and LAMA
notes: Montelukast blocks leukotriene D4 receptor. Add-on, helps allergic rhinitis, viral wheeze, **exercise asthma**. **Black box: mood changes, aggression, suicidal thoughts**.
**LAMA (tiotropium)**: add-on to ICS-LABA for moderate to severe, over 6 years. Side effects: dry mouth.

sections.title: Exacerbation severity
notes: Mild to moderate: talks in phrases, not agitated, **sats over 90%, peak flow over 50%**.
Severe: **talks in words**, hunched, agitated, accessory muscles, pulsus paradoxus over 20, **sats under 90%, peak flow under 50%**.
Life-threatening: **silent chest**, drowsy, confused, exhausted.

sections.title: Home and office management of exacerbations
notes: Written **asthma action plan**. AIR or more salbutamol. In 6 to 11 year olds, **doubling the inhaled steroid alone doesn't help**.
Oral steroids 3 to 5 days if no response to reliever in 2 to 3 days or peak flow under 60%.
Office: **salbutamol 4 to 10 puffs with spacer every 20 minutes x 3**, **prednisone 1 to 2 mg/kg (max 40)**, oxygen to sats 94 to 98%. Reassess at 1 hour, discharge if well, follow up in 1 to 2 days.
Severe or worsening: transfer to ED, add **ipratropium**.

sections.title: Stepwise therapy (GINA 2023)
notes: Ages 6 to 11: symptoms under twice a month: SABA plus low-dose ICS. Twice a month or more: **daily low-dose ICS**.
Most days or waking once a week: low or medium ICS, low ICS-LABA, or very low ICS-formoterol MART.
Daily or with low lung function: medium ICS-LABA or low ICS-formoterol MART, refer. Uncontrolled: specialist, biologics.
12 and over: **as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol (AIR)** at step 1 to 2, then ICS-formoterol MART at increasing doses, then add LAMA.

sections.title: Case: still coughing on fluticasone
notes: 6-year-old using fluticasone correctly plus montelukast, still coughing: **switch to ICS-formoterol daily and as needed**, don't just raise the fluticasone dose.

sections.title: Asthma under 5 years
notes: Rule out other causes (congenital lung disease). Likely asthma: over 10 days of cough, wheeze with **more than 3 URIs a year**, night symptoms, **symptoms between colds**, atopy.
Step 1: SABA plus **low-dose ICS at the start of each viral illness**. Step 2: daily low-dose ICS for 3 months. Step 3: check diagnosis and technique, double ICS, refer.

sections.title: Risk of asthma death
notes: **More than 1 salbutamol canister a month**, non-Hispanic Black, **previous intubation** (single strongest predictor), hospital or ED visit in the past year, recent oral steroids.

sections.title: Severe exacerbation and impending failure
notes: Case: 7-year-old talking in words, sats 88%, retractions: **send to the ED**.
Paradoxical breathing, **silent chest, bradycardia**, pulsus paradoxus disappears (fatigue), confusion. **Normal or rising CO2** is a bad sign.
Status asthmaticus: admit, fluids, oxygen, **continuous salbutamol**, ipratropium, IV steroids, **magnesium sulfate**.
